summary: Code the existing first-order syntax and proof rules, with finite certificates for enumerable axioms, and prove that checking a proof is primitive recursive.
abstract: A proof can be checked one inference at a time, even when finding it took considerable ingenuity. To make that distinction precise, we record expressions and finite proofs by natural numbers. The codes retain the difference between free variables, bound positions and temporary witness names, so substitution and freshness conditions can be checked mechanically. A theory whose axioms are gradually enumerated presents an extra difficulty: a checker cannot simply wait to discover whether a proposed assumption is an axiom. We attach a finite certificate to each such assumption instead. The result is a primitive-recursive check that accepts exactly the finite proofs of the earlier first-order calculus. This turns provability into a question about the existence of a numerical certificate.
